title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Persons with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company (Key Management Personnel, including directors), employees of the Group, and Connected Persons of KMP/Employees. All substantive prohibitions and clearance requirements apply uniformly to this tier.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Employees of the Group; distinguished only for clearance (Managing Director and Chair, or Company Secretary in their absence).

tiers.name: Director (other than the Managing Director)
tiers.description: Non-executive/other directors; distinguished only for clearance (the Chair and the Managing Director).

tiers.name: Managing Director
tiers.description: Managing Director; distinguished only for clearance (the Chair and a Non-Executive Director, or the Finance Director in both their absences).

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: Chair of the Board; distinguished only for clearance (the Managing Director and a Non-Executive Director).

tiers.name: Connected Person
tiers.description: Spouse or partner; child or step-child under 18; a parent; an unlisted body corporate the KMP/Employee controls or directs; a trust of which they or the above are trustee or beneficiary; or any other person over whom they have significant influence or control.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes

windows.start_anchor: five trading days before the meeting of the full Board (as Audit Committee) for approval of half-year or annual financial accounts
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the Company's half year and annual financial accounts

windows.start_anchor: the quarter-end at which the quarterly mining/exploration activity report and Appendix 5B are compiled
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after release of the quarterly mining/exploration activity report and Appendix 5B

windows.start_anchor: release of an announcement by the Company
windows.end_anchor: close of the next trading date after the day the announcement is released

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may impose an 'Additional Period' from time to time, for example while considering matters requiring disclosure but for Listing Rule 3.1A. Confidential: Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.

rules.detail: Company Securities expressly includes derivatives of shares/options (equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or OTC options), whether cash or physically settled, with no venue limit. Trading such a derivative is a 'trade' (apply for/acquire/dispose, or agree to do so) requiring prior written clearance under section 7, and is barred during a Prohibited Period without exceptional-circumstances clearance.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route referenced, on transactions limiting the economic risk of unvested equity-based remuneration entitlements.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested shares (or non-plan shares) is not separately named. A put/call over such shares is caught only because it is a trade in a Company Security (derivative), requiring prior written clearance and subject to Prohibited Periods.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above ... whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. prepaid forward) is not named. It falls within 'trade' as an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities, so it requires prior written clearance and is barred in a Prohibited Period absent exceptional-circumstances clearance.
rules.evidence: enter into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities

rules.detail: Unconditional ban on borrowing or selling Company Securities intending to buy back later; the clearance acknowledgement form separately confirms this is treated as an absolutely prohibited activity, not one that clearance can excuse.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into agreements, transactions or instruments to borrow or sell Company Securities with an intention of buying those Company Securities back at a later date, a practice commonly known as short selling.

rules.detail: Lending out Company Securities (as distinct from borrowing to short sell) is not named anywhere and is not within the 'trade' definition.
CFDs are not named but fall within 'derivatives ... whether settled by cash or otherwise', so entering one over Company Securities is a trade requiring prior written clearance.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Margin loan agreements over Company Securities require prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer; a subsequent forced sale by the lender is excluded from the Prohibited Period restrictions (section 8(g)).
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

rules.detail: Granting security is captured as 'other secured lending arrangements' and requires the same prior written clearance as a margin loan; not addressed via the general trade/dealing definition.
rules.evidence: or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer

rules.detail: Section 10 permits any secured lending arrangement over Company Securities with prior written clearance and no stated exclusion by tier or vesting state. The attached clearance acknowledgement form, however, lists 'obtaining margin loans ... or enter[ing] into any other secured financing arrangements' among conduct the signatory affirms is prohibited under the policy, an internal inconsistency that should be resolved with the Company before relying on the clearance route.
rules.evidence: I will not engage in activity that is prohibited in the Company's Securities Trading Policy, including but not limited to short selling of the Company Securities, obtaining margin loans using Company Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security for loans or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Acquiring shares intending to dispose within under 3 months requires prior written clearance; disposing shortly after vesting/issuance under a share plan is expressly carved out.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not acquire Company Securities with the intention of disposing of some or all of those Company Securities within a period of less than 3 months from the date of the acquisition without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 7.

clearance.approver: Managing Director and the Chairman, or the other in the absence of one, or the Company Secretary if both are absent
clearance.evidence: in the case of employees, the Managing Director and the Chairman, or in the absence of one of these Approving Officers, the other Approving Officer, or in both of their absences, the Company Secretary

clearance.approver: the Chair and the Managing Director, or the other in the absence of one
clearance.evidence: in the case of a director (other than the Managing Director), the Chair and the Managing Director, or in the absence of one of these Approving Officers, the other Approving Officer

clearance.approver: the Chair and a Non-Executive Director, or the other in the absence of one, or the Finance Director if both are absent
clearance.evidence: in the case of the Managing Director, the Chair and a Non-Executive Director, or in the absence of one of these Approving Officers, the other Approving Officer, or in both of their absences, the Finance Director

clearance.approver: the Managing Director and a Non-Executive Director
clearance.evidence: in the case of the Chair, the Managing Director and a Non-Executive Director

carve_outs: disposing of Company Securities within a short time period after vesting or issuance of the Company Securities under a share plan
short_term.evidence: Restricted Persons must not acquire Company Securities with the intention of disposing of some or all of those Company Securities within a period of less than 3 months from the date of the acquisition without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer

exceptions.evidence: transfers of Company Securities between a Restricted Person and their spouse, civil partner, child, step-child, family company, family trust or other close family member or of Company Securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

trading in the Company Securities by that trust provided that the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Prohibited Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer
a disposal of Company Securities arising from a scheme of arrangement

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board
a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
the exercise (but not the sale of Company Securities following exercise) of an option or right under an employee incentive scheme that is ASIC Class Order 03/1874 compliant

trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... and where ... the trading plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade
a director obtaining a share qualification
A person may be in severe financial hardship if he or she has a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the relevant Company Securities.

the person in question is required by a court order or a court enforceable undertaking to transfer or sell, or accept a transfer of, the Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for him or her to do so

exemption_authority: The Approving Officer relevant to the person's role (see clearance) may grant prior written clearance to trade during a Prohibited Period for severe financial hardship or other circumstances the Approving Officer deems exceptional (section 6). The Approving Officer has absolute discretion to refuse, which is final and binding, and the refusal is confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities, including for the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 6, unless the Restricted Person first obtains prior written clearance ... A written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of 5 business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that only require clearance in blackout periods, RXL requires fresh 5-business-day written clearance for every dealing at any time, so entry, unwind and settlement of a collar each need separate, freshly-timed approvals.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The clearance acknowledgement form states the signatory 'will not engage in activity that is prohibited ... including ... obtaining margin loans ... or enter into any other secured financing arrangements', while section 10 of the policy body permits such arrangements with prior written clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This drafting inconsistency creates real risk that Approving Officers administer the form as an absolute ban; the bank should obtain company confirmation that section 10's clearance route (not the form's blanket wording) governs before structuring the loan leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement ... is excluded from the restrictions outlined in section 5
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default is excluded from the Prohibited Period ban, giving a clean enforcement path even during a blackout or confidential Additional Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must do that act or thing in respect of the Connected Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not avoid the clearance and secured-lending requirements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The express hedging ban is confined to unvested plan entitlements, so a collar over already-vested shares is not caught by section 9 and falls back to the general clearance regime instead.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank may not be told why a clearance request for collar execution is delayed or refused, complicating timing certainty for trade entry.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted RXL shares is achievable in principle but every step needs prior written clearance from the relevant Approving Officer, because Company Securities expressly includes exchange-traded and OTC derivatives and clearance is required for all dealing, not just during Prohibited Periods. The hedging ban in section 9 applies only to unvested equity incentive entitlements, so it does not block a collar over vested shares. Section 10 permits the loan leg (margin loan or other secured lending arrangement) with the same prior written clearance, and a lender's forced sale on default is excluded from Prohibited Period restrictions, giving the bank a clear enforcement path; however, the policy's own clearance acknowledgement form separately describes secured financing arrangements as prohibited conduct, an inconsistency that should be resolved with the Company before relying on section 10. Short selling is banned outright with no clearance override, and each clearance lapses after 5 business days, so entry, rolls and unwind must be re-cleared each time and kept clear of Prohibited Periods and any confidential Additional Period.
